content.text:
**M1 is shipped — all four phases, everything green, working tree clean.** A directory can now be backed up to CISS and restored byte-identically with `ciss-ctl sync backup <dir>` / `sync restore <dir>`, uploading only chunks the server lacks.

Phase 3 closed out the ladder: the roundtrip flow test proves backup→wipe→restore is byte-identical (content + mode + mtime), a substituted chunk fails closed with the cid and path named and nothing written, and a cold restore with zero local state discovers the fs-manifest from the keep-set by its `kind` self-tag among decoy small leaves. The live drills against a real server binary confirmed all of it, including an at-rest byte-flip on a stored block: the server's C2 invariant refused it with a 500 before the client's own verification even saw the bytes, the previously-verified file stayed intact, and the tampered file never appeared.

Final state on `ciss-sync` (12 commits, nothing pushed):

- `410fd9b` Phase 1 — the `ciss-sync` crate: FastCDC 64K/256K/1M dual-hash chunking, canonical DAG-CBOR `FsManifest`, scanner + sqlite fast-path index
- `8348a58` Phase 2 — transport seams, backup with have/want via `du`, G3 cid guard, keep-set under I5, `Client::put_manifest`/`get_manifest`, tracing + the pre-transfer pricing line
- `3d21f8c` Phase 3 — verified restore, per-file verify-before-rename atomicity, cold discovery, `sync restore`
- Plan doc is CLOSED with the full Outcome Summary, per-phase delivered notes, and a close-out entry recording six execution discoveries — most notably that the mutation audit caught the tuning constants unpinned (the golden digest now covers params + boundaries), and that the foundations review's `kind` self-tag turned out to be the load-bearing cold-discovery mechanism, not just domain separation.

Gates at close: 53 workspace test suites green, clippy-pedantic 0 warnings, cargo-mutants 34 caught / 0 missed on the chunker + codec.

Worth knowing for next steps: M2 (bounded local footprint) is the next milestone in the ladder, and the parent milestone plan now marks M1 shipped. Say the word if you want the branch pushed or a PR opened.

gh pr create --repo CroftCommunity/CISS --base main --head ciss-sync --title "File-sync M1: chunk core + backup/restore (ciss-sync crate, ciss-ctl sync)" --body "## Summary

Delivers **M1 of the file-sync client** (\`docs/plans/2026-08-07-file-sync-client.md\`): *back up a directory to CISS and restore it byte-identical*, one device + the helper server, uploading only the chunks the server lacks.

- **\`ciss-sync\` crate (new)** — the pure sync engine: FastCDC content-defined chunking (avg 256 KiB, max 1 MiB under the 2 MiB object cap) with dual sha-256/blake3 \`ChunkRef\`s hashed in one pass; the canonical DAG-CBOR \`FsManifest\` led by a \`kind: croft.fs-manifest/v1\` self-tag, \`content_id\` = the server's own cid derivation (C1); deterministic scanner + a minimal mtime/size sqlite fast-path index; \`BlobTransport\`/\`ManifestSlot\` transport seams; backup and verified-restore flows.
- **\`ciss-ctl sync backup <dir>\`** — scan, have/want via \`du\`, upload missing chunks + the fs-manifest, commit the keep-set \`Manifest\` at \`last+1\` under I5. Server-assigned cid must equal the local sha-256 (G3) or the transfer is refused. Interrupted backups never half-commit and resume by skipping stored chunks.
- **\`ciss-ctl sync restore <dir> [--manifest <cid>]\`** — every chunk verified against its address at the engine layer; per-file verify-before-rename atomicity (a tampered chunk names its cid + path and writes nothing); cold restore discovers the fs-manifest from the keep-set by the kind tag. mode + mtime restored (mtime as a replayed assertion, never ordering).
- **\`Client\` gains \`put_manifest\`/\`get_manifest\`** (the manifest is self-authorizing: \`x-croft-pubkey\` only); \`ciss-ctl\` gains an \`EnvFilter\` tracing init (default \`warn\`) with per-chunk have/want decisions at DEBUG and a pre-transfer pricing line at INFO (the M5 cost-twin embryo).
- Plan docs: phase-plan Passes 1–3, a foundations/corpus review (Drystone/Croft tie-in with owned deviations), per-phase delivered notes, and a close-out.

Server-side behavior is unchanged (one \`clippy\`-driven \`map_or\` rewrite in \`now_unix_s\`, semantics identical).

## Test plan

- TDD throughout — every integrity guard landed RED-first: chunk caps + tiling, golden \`content_id\` + golden boundary/param digest, dual-hash vs the server's own sha-256, keep-set-under-I5 with the stale-seq refusal surfaced, server-cid==local (G3), tampered-chunk-rejected, interrupted-resume, cold discovery among decoy leaves.
- \`cargo test --workspace\`: 53 suites green. \`cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace\` (pedantic): 0 warnings.
- \`cargo mutants\` on the chunker + codec: 34 caught / 5 unviable / 0 missed.
- Live drills against a real server binary: 10-chunk backup, \`skipped=10\` re-run, cold-restore \`diff -r\` clean with mtime restored, and an at-rest byte-flip refused (server C2 + client verify; verified file intact, tampered file never written).

content.text:
**Done: PR #14 merged into `main`, branch deleted, local `main` synced.** M1 is on mainline.

## What's next

**The milestone ladder** (from `docs/plans/2026-08-07-file-sync-client.md`):

- **M2 — bounded local footprint** is next: a content-addressed local cache with a size budget (a chunk is always safe to evict — re-fetchable by hash), LRU + pin policy, and online-only placeholders that hydrate on access. No server change. The sqlite index from Phase 1 is the natural seed for this.
- **M3 — two-device converge** is the real prize: `DeviceHead` + `Frontier{heads}`, the client-side fold with conflict-copy, and the ladder's *only* server change (the additive owner-signed `Manifest.heads` field under I5). The M1 spine was built so this lands on tested ground.
- M4 (iroh peer-fetch — the blake3 half of every `ChunkRef` is already waiting) and M5 (cost twin — the pre-transfer pricing line is its embryo) follow.

**Three things I'd flag before or alongside M2:**

1. **CISS has no CI.** There is no `.github/workflows/` in this repo, so PR #14 merged on local gates only — that's exactly the gap the workspace `CI-PATTERN.md` warns about ("a workflow without a `pull_request` trigger is a notification, not a gate"). A small workflow running `cargo test --workspace` + `cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace` on every PR and push to main, per the croft-pwa reference pattern, is high value for an hour of work. I'd do this first.
2. **Discovery-repo housekeeping:** ROADMAP_TODO E90 should get an "M1 shipped 2026-08-07" stamp, and the foundations review surfaced a wording reconciliation for E90 (its "bsky app-token" auth line vs the structural need for the namespace key on the write path). COHESION §67 could take a one-line status note too.
3. **A `ciss-ctl` release** would put `sync backup`/`restore` in your hands on the deployed box: version bump + tag + homebrew formula update in the tap (following the release conventions). Also worth noting: the CLI currently runs backups without the scan index (engine supports it; the CLI passes `None`), so every backup re-chunks — correct but not the fast path. Wiring a default index location into the CLI is a small M2-adjacent task.

There's also the standing E89 lane from the corpus review: restore today is a metered, gated read, and the "exit is unconditionally cap-exempt" rule remains an unbuilt candidate CISS invariant — M1's roundtrip drill exercises exactly the path that ADR would exempt, so the evidence for writing it now exists.

My recommendation for the next session: CI gate first, then M2 as its own phase-planned branch.

| E88 | **arecipe cookbook durability — copy recipes into the cookbook owner's PDS vs reference the author's (2026-08-06)** — raised by the user while planning arecipe's bundled-snapshot work. **Current state (verified 2026-08-06):** a cookbook is a **pure reference set**. `app.arecipe.cookFollow` stores only `{ subject: <followed cook's DID>, createdAt }` (`docs/LEXICONS.md`; `src/social/cook-follows-pds.ts`); recipes are read live from each author's repo (`src/recipes/read.ts` `createRecipeReader`, `src/pages/browse.ts` `entriesByDid`). **Nothing copies a recipe into the follower's repo** — `write.ts` create/putRecord is for authoring your own. **Failure modes this exposes:** an author deleting a recipe, deactivating, migrating PDS, or going offline silently removes content from *your* cookbook — and the app **actively prunes** it (`revalidate.ts` 4xx → `'gone'` → `browse.ts` `onGone` drops the cook from the live view). Your curation survives; the content does not. **The tension:** copying buys durability + offline completeness, but (a) forks provenance, (b) duplicates storage across every follower, (c) raises licence questions — the Wikibooks corpus is CC BY-SA 4.0 and **O3 chose fork-on-edit**, so a copy is a derivative that must carry lineage (`RUN-WIKIBOOKS-CORPUS-SUMMARY.md`), and (d) needs a staleness story if the author later edits. **Shape questions:** copy-on-add vs copy-on-demand ("pin"/"save" gesture); whether a copy is a *distinct* record (e.g. `app.arecipe.savedRecipe` = snapshot + source ref + retrieved-at, keeping "mine" and "saved" separable) or a full `exchange.recipe.recipe` in your own repo (durable but muddies authorship in Browse/Cookbook); and whether the existing `attribution`/`sourceUrl`/`sourcePermalink` provenance fields already carry enough lineage to make a copy honest. **Note the parallel:** the 2026-08-06 bundled-snapshot plan already copies the corpus **into the client** for exactly this durability/offline instinct — same motivation, different layer (device cache vs the user's own PDS). # CI pattern — workspace-wide

**Canonical writeup: `croft-pwa/docs/CI.md`.** That repo is the reference
implementation; this file is the workspace-level index — what the pattern is in
one screen, which repos currently satisfy it, and what to check when adding CI to
a new one.

Lives in `.claude/` rather than loose at the `CroftC/` root deliberately: the
meta-repo tracks only `.claude/` + `.gitignore` (see `CLAUDE.md` → "Repo content
belongs in its repo"), and `.claude/` is auto-loaded for agent sessions working
anywhere under `CroftC/` — which is exactly the reach a cross-repo convention
wants.

## The shape

Two jobs. A **gate** on every PR *and* every push to `main`; a **deploy** that
runs only on `main`, only after the gate passes.

```
  PR opened ──► gate ──✗──► blocked before it reaches main
       │
       └─ merge ──► push:main ──► gate ──✓──► deploy
                                    └──✗──► no deploy, main flagged
```

Nine rules, each preventing a specific failure (full reasoning in
`croft-pwa/docs/CI.md`):

1. **`on:` includes `pull_request`** — otherwise nothing runs until the commit is
   already on `main`. The gate protects the deploy but not the branch, and the PR
   reports `mergeable: MERGEABLE, checks: 0` — clean because nothing ran.
2. **`deploy: needs: <gate>`** — a red gate must block publication, not annotate it.
3. **`deploy: if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`** — `workflow_dispatch` can be
   aimed at any ref; without the guard, dispatching a branch publishes it to
   production.
4. **`concurrency` scoped so a PR run cannot cancel a production deploy** — per-ref
   group, or scoped to the publishing job.
5. **`permissions: contents: read`** at workflow level, elevated only on the job
   that publishes.
6. **One gate command, identical locally and in CI** (`npm test`, `npm run
   test:rust`) — so there is no "passed on my machine" variant to argue with.
7. **Every toolchain pinned in-repo and resolved explicitly, not off `PATH`** —
   *and enforced*, see below.
8. **Every job has a `timeout-minutes`** — otherwise it inherits GitHub's
   six-hour default, and a test that *hangs* rather than fails sits there for all
   of it. In `fun` a hung vitest worker produced "every test passed, run failed",
   which is not a shape anyone reads quickly.
9. **A manual path exists (`workflow_dispatch`) and can actually publish** —
   GitHub throttled *webhook deliveries* during the 2026-08-06 Actions incident,
   so pushes stopped triggering runs for hours and dispatch was the only way to
   gate or deploy. Publish steps are conditioned `!= 'pull_request'`, never
   `== 'push'` (that mismatch made `fun`'s dispatch skip its artifact upload and
   then fail looking for it). **Pull the hatch once** — an escape hatch nobody has
   opened is a comment, not a hatch.

## Rule 7 is the one that bites silently

The others fail loudly the first time. This one produces **green locally, red in
CI, on code you did not touch** — and it cost three round trips in `fun` before
anyone looked at the version numbers:
ci.yml
preview.yml

anyone looked at the version numbers:

> Homebrew's `cargo-clippy` shadowed rustup's on `PATH` **and lagged** — local
> 0.1.94, CI 0.1.97. Every "clean" local run was a different program. A scrubbed
> `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` ruled out caching and still disagreed.

Both halves are needed: pin the version (`rust-toolchain.toml`, `.nvmrc`) **and**
resolve the binary explicitly (`rustup which` from the repo root, `setup-node`
with `node-version-file`). Pinning alone still lets a shadowing `PATH` win.

**A third half, learned 2026-08-06: declaring the pin is not enforcing it.**
`fun` had `.nvmrc` (22) *and* `engines: ">=22 <23"`, and a developer ran the whole
suite on Node 25 for a day anyway — `engines` only **warns**, and the warning
scrolls past `npm ci`. Eleven failures were carried for hours as "known,
pre-existing, green on CI". Add `engine-strict=true` to `.npmrc` so npm
**refuses**, and name the version manager that reads the pin (`fnm` +
`--use-on-cd`) so the refusal has an obvious remedy. Verify it in both directions
when you add it — `engine-strict` also applies to dependencies' ranges.

The full ladder: **declare (`.nvmrc`) · read (`setup-node`) · refuse
(`engine-strict`) · resolve (a version manager).**

## Current state (audited 2026-08-05, refreshed 2026-08-07)

| repo | workflows | `pull_request` | ref-guard | concurrency | timeouts | dispatch | pin enforced |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| croft-pwa | 2 | 2 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| fun | 1 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| arecipe | 2 | 2 | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
| discovery | 2 | 2 | — | ✓ | — | — | — |
| greetings_site | 2 | 2 | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
| skylite | 3 | 2 | — | ✓ | — | — | — |
| pdsview | 2 | 1 | — | ✓ | — | — | — |
| view | 2 | 1 | ✓ | — | — | — | — |
| croft-stack | 1 | **0** | — | — | — | — | — |
| arecipe_treatise · CISS · crofting_site · experiments · graze · stellin | — | | | | | | |

**`fun` and `croft-pwa` now satisfy all nine**; the 2026-08-05 audit's two
outliers are down to one (`croft-stack`). The three new columns are unaudited
elsewhere — they are new rules, so a blank means "not checked", not "known bad".

Repos with no workflows are not automatically a gap: several are content or

# reasoning in croft-pwa/docs/CI.md). Gate on every PR and every push to main;
# there is no deploy job here — deployment lives in croft-stack.
#
# The gate runs the same two commands the repo gates on locally (CLAUDE.md):

#   cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace   (pedantic; warnings are errors here)
# Note: no cargo fmt — deliberate, see CLAUDE.md ("do not run cargo fmt").

name: ci

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Manual escape hatch (rule 9) — exercised once at setup so it is known to work.
  workflow_dispatch:

# CISS file-sync — M2 execution plan (bounded local footprint)

date: 2026-08-07
status: **Planned (condensed three-pass, single context — moderate scope on settled M1 ground). EXECUTING.**
parent: `docs/plans/2026-08-07-file-sync-client.md` (milestone ladder; this doc executes **M2**).
skill: authored under the `phase-plan` workflow (abbreviated passes — see Review Log).

## Problem Statement

Deliver **M2**: *"local footprint is bounded regardless of logical tree size."* After M1, a backed-up
tree's bytes all live locally AND on the server. M2 lets a device **evict** cold files (drop the local
bytes, keep the logical entry) and **hydrate** them back on demand — so the logical tree can be larger
than the disk it syncs from. Server change: **none.** The dangerous edge is silent data loss: an evicted
file must never fall out of the fs-manifest/keep-set (a later backup that "forgets" evicted entries would
GC their chunks server-side), and eviction must be refused unless the bytes are provably on the server.

## Reasoning

**Placeholders are state-records, not stub files.** An evicted file is *absent from disk* and recorded in
the sync state DB. Rejected: zero-byte stub files (they masquerade as real empty files to every other
program — silent corruption by another name) and xattr/sparse tricks (platform-specific, M4+ concern).
"Hydrate on access" without a VFS layer means an explicit `sync hydrate` (FUSE/File Provider integration
is out of scope for a CLI milestone; the engine API is what a future VFS would call).

**The logical tree = scanned files ∪ placeholders.** `backup` must merge placeholder entries into the
manifest it commits — this is the no-data-loss invariant, and it lands RED-first before any evict code
exists. A file that reappears locally wins over its placeholder (the placeholder is dropped).

**The chunk cache is the footprint dial and the M4/M5 seam.** Evict may spill chunks into a budgeted
content-addressed cache (cheap re-hydrate, zero metered egress); hydrate reads through it (cache hit =
no server fetch = no download receipt — the economics are observable and tested). LRU + pinned flag;
"starred/working-set" pin *policies* stay M3+ — the mechanism (a pin bit) ships now.

**A per-tree state root** (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/ciss-ctl/sync/<tree-id>/`, `--state-dir` override; `tree-id` =
sha-256 of profile + canonical path, first 16 hex) holds the scan index (M1's, now actually wired into the
CLI), the placeholder table, config (cache budget), and the cache dir. The state root must live outside
the tree (M1 learning: scanning your own mutating sqlite poisons the manifest).

## Verified Assumptions

- M1 base (all shipped, `docs/plans/2026-08-07-file-sync-m1-chunk-and-backup.md`): `scan_tree_indexed` +
  `Index` (hit/miss counters); `BlobTransport`/`ManifestSlot` seams; `verify_content` engine-layer check;
  restore's per-file verify-before-rename materializer (Phase 3 refactors it into a shared helper —
  hydrate is restore-for-one-file); `backup` flow at `backup.rs` (Phase 2 inserts the placeholder merge).
- `ciss-cli/src/config.rs` resolves `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`$HOME/.config` manually — the data-dir resolution
  mirrors it (`$XDG_DATA_HOME`/`$HOME/.local/share`), no new dependency.
- No new crates: rusqlite/sha2/serde/tracing all present in `ciss-sync`.

## Documentation Impact

- `README.md` — `sync evict|hydrate|status` lines in the client section. **Phase 3.**
- `docs/plans/2026-08-07-file-sync-client.md` — M2 status stamp at close-out. **Phase 3.**
- Module docs in new `ciss-sync` files (`state.rs`, `cache.rs`, `placeholder.rs`, `hydrate.rs`). **Each phase.**

## Concurrency Map

**All phases sequential** (each builds on the prior's write-set in `crates/ciss-sync/**`). No worktrees.

## Phases

### Phase 1: state root + chunk cache + placeholder store (pure)
**Goal:** the three storage primitives, fully unit-tested offline.
**Changes:**
- [ ] `state.rs`: `SyncState::open(state_dir)` — one sqlite (`state.sqlite`: scan_index [reuse `Index`
  schema], placeholders, config KV) + `cache/` dir; `tree_id(profile, path)` helper.
- [ ] `cache.rs`: `ChunkCache` — `insert(cid, bytes)`, `get(cid) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` (verified against
  cid on read — a corrupt cache entry is deleted + treated as a miss, fail-safe not fail-open),
  `pin/unpin(cid)`, budget enforcement on insert: evict LRU unpinned until `total ≤ budget`; a single
  blob larger than the budget is refused, never stored-then-immediately-evicted.
- [ ] `placeholder.rs`: `PlaceholderStore` — `record(path, &FileEntry)`, `remove(path)`, `get(path)`,
  `all() -> BTreeMap<String, FileEntry>` (entry serialized as DAG-CBOR, like the index).
**Test-first order (RED → GREEN):** `cache_budget_lru` (inserts beyond budget evict oldest-accessed
unpinned; pinned survive; get refreshes recency; edges: exact-budget fit, oversize refusal, budget 0),
`cache_corrupt_entry_is_a_miss` (flip a byte in a cached file → get returns None and removes it),
`placeholder_roundtrip` (record/get/all/remove; entries survive reopen), `state_reopen` (config KV +
tables persist).
**Wiring test:** crate-level `crates/ciss-sync/tests/state_cache.rs` through the public API only
(pure-lib phase; CLI wiring is Phases 2–3).
**Done when:** `cargo test -p ciss-sync` green incl. the new suites.
**Validation:** Narrow — unit + crate-integration sufficient. Mutation audit: `cargo mutants` scoped to
`cache.rs` (the LRU/budget boundary logic) once green.

### Phase 2: evict + placeholder-aware backup (`sync evict`, `sync status`)
**Goal:** drop a file's local bytes safely; the logical tree survives every later backup.
**Changes:**
- [ ] `evict.rs`: `evict(dir, state, server, paths) -> EvictReport` — per file: entry from the current
  scan; **refuse unless every chunk cid is in the server's have-set AND in the committed keep-set
  manifest** (both: `have` proves the bytes exist, the keep-set proves billing/GC protection); spill
  chunks into the cache within budget (best-effort, never a failure); record placeholder; delete the
  file. INFO per eviction (path, bytes freed, chunks cached); ERROR naming the unbacked chunks on refusal.
- [ ] `backup.rs`: merge `PlaceholderStore::all()` into the scanned manifest (file-on-disk wins and drops
  its placeholder; placeholder fills in for an absent file) — the manifest/keep-set never shrinks from an
  eviction. `backup` gains an optional `&SyncState` (index + placeholders together).
- [ ] CLI: `sync evict <dir> <path>...`, `sync status <dir>` (present/evicted per file, cache usage vs
  budget, keep-set seq); `sync backup` now opens the state root by default (wires M1's index in —
  `--state-dir` override, `--no-state` opt-out).
**Test-first order (RED → GREEN):** flow `tests/flow_sync_footprint.rs` —
1. `backup_preserves_evicted_entries` (**the no-data-loss guard, RED-first**): backup → evict a file →
   backup again → the new fs-manifest still contains the evicted entry; the keep-set still names all its
   chunks; local file absent.
2. `evict_refuses_unbacked_file` (**integrity guard**): a file modified after its last backup (or never
   backed up) is refused with the unbacked chunk cids named; the file is untouched.
3. `evicted_file_restores_cleanly`: M1's `restore` of the tree elsewhere still reproduces the evicted
   file byte-identically (server-side truth unaffected by local eviction).
**Done when:** `cargo test -p ciss --test flow_sync_footprint` green; behavioral: after evict, local
bytes shrink, `sync status` shows the file as evicted, and a re-backup changes nothing server-side.
**Validation:** Moderate — flow + unit + a live CLI pass (evict against the real server, `sync status`,
re-backup, `du` unchanged).

### Phase 3: hydrate (`sync hydrate`) + the footprint capability end-to-end
**Goal:** bytes come back on demand — from the cache when possible, the server when not — verified.
**Changes:**
- [ ] Refactor restore's per-file materializer (fetch chunks → verify each → assemble → verify size →
  tmp-write → mode/mtime → rename) into a shared `materialize.rs` used by both `restore` and `hydrate`
  (no drift between the two verified-write paths).
- [ ] `hydrate.rs`: `hydrate(dir, state, server, paths|all) -> HydrateReport` — per placeholder: chunks
  via cache read-through (hit = no server fetch; miss = `transport.get` + populate cache within budget),
  materialize, drop the placeholder, refresh the index. **Refuses to overwrite an existing file** (a
  reappeared file wins; fail loud, never clobber).
- [ ] CLI: `sync hydrate <dir> [<path>...]` (default: all placeholders); README + milestone-plan doc
  updates.
**Test-first order (RED → GREEN):** extend `flow_sync_footprint.rs` —
4. `footprint_bounded_while_tree_grows` (**the M2 capability gate**): tree larger than the budget →
   backup → evict to fit → local bytes ≤ budget while the keep-set covers the whole tree → hydrate one
   file → byte-identical (content + mode + mtime).
5. `cache_hit_hydrate_fetches_nothing` (a counting transport wrapper): evict with cache spill → hydrate
   → zero `get` calls reach the server (the metered-egress win, observable).
6. `eviction_never_loses_data`: evict, wipe the cache entirely → hydrate refetches from the server and
   verifies (M1's tamper guard inherited via the shared materializer).
7. `hydrate_refuses_overwrite`: place a new file at an evicted path → hydrate refuses; the file is
   untouched; backup prefers the on-disk file and drops the placeholder.
**Done when:** the full flow suite green; behavioral: a directory whose logical size exceeds local disk
budget round-trips through evict → status → hydrate with every byte verified.
**Validation:** Moderate — flow + unit + a live drill: real server, evict a big file, `sync hydrate`,
`diff`; then wipe the cache and hydrate again (server path). Mutation audit: `cache.rs` +
`placeholder.rs` survivors triaged.

## Open Questions — resolved by default (user delegated execution 2026-08-07; overrides welcome)

- **Placeholder representation** — RESOLVED: absent file + state-DB record (stubs masquerade; see
  Reasoning). *ADVISORY.*
- **State root location** — RESOLVED: `$XDG_DATA_HOME/ciss-ctl/sync/<tree-id>/` (mirrors config.rs's
  XDG resolution), `--state-dir` override. *ADVISORY.*
- **Cache budget default** — RESOLVED: 256 MiB, persisted in state config, `--cache-budget` to change.
  *ADVISORY.*
- **Pin policy scope** — RESOLVED: the pin *mechanism* (bit + never-evict) ships; recent/starred/
  working-set *policies* deferred to M3+ where the working set becomes observable. *ADVISORY.*

## Review Log

- **2026-08-07 (abbreviated passes, one context)** — Pass 1: plan authored from the milestone M2 slice on
  shipped M1 ground. Pass 2 checks folded in: placeholder-merge is in `backup.rs` (not a wrapper) so every
  caller inherits it; evict requires *both* have-set and keep-set membership; the cache verifies on read
  (fail-safe); hydrate shares restore's materializer (single verified-write path); state root outside the
  tree (M1 learning). Pass 3 gates: every guard named RED-first above (no-data-loss, refuse-unbacked,
  budget/LRU, corrupt-cache-is-miss, refuse-overwrite, cache-hit-zero-fetch); tracing spec'd per flow;
  validation calibrated (narrow/moderate/moderate); concurrency map all-sequential; docs scheduled in the
  phases that stale them; mutation target `cache.rs`+`placeholder.rs`.

- [ ] CLI: `sync evict <dir> <path>...`, `sync status <dir>` (present/evicted per file, cache usage vs
  budget, keep-set seq); `sync backup` now opens the state root by default (wires M1's index in —
  `--state-dir` override, `--no-state` opt-out).
**Test-first order (RED → GREEN):** flow `tests/flow_sync_footprint.rs` —
1. `backup_preserves_evicted_entries` (**the no-data-loss guard, RED-first**): backup → evict a file →
   backup again → the new fs-manifest still contains the evicted entry; the keep-set still names all its
   chunks; local file absent.
2. `evict_refuses_unbacked_file` (**integrity guard**): a file modified after its last backup (or never
   backed up) is refused with the unbacked chunk cids named; the file is untouched.
3. `evicted_file_restores_cleanly`: M1's `restore` of the tree elsewhere still reproduces the evicted
   file byte-identically (server-side truth unaffected by local eviction).
**Done when:** `cargo test -p ciss --test flow_sync_footprint` green; behavioral: after evict, local
bytes shrink, `sync status` shows the file as evicted, and a re-backup changes nothing server-side.
**Validation:** Moderate — flow + unit + a live CLI pass (evict against the real server, `sync status`,
re-backup, `du` unchanged).

### Phase 3: hydrate (`sync hydrate`) + the footprint capability end-to-end
**Goal:** bytes come back on demand — from the cache when possible, the server when not — verified.
**Changes:**
- [ ] Refactor restore's per-file materializer (fetch chunks → verify each → assemble → verify size →
  tmp-write → mode/mtime → rename) into a shared `materialize.rs` used by both `restore` and `hydrate`
  (no drift between the two verified-write paths).
- [ ] `hydrate.rs`: `hydrate(dir, state, server, paths|all) -> HydrateReport` — per placeholder: chunks
  via cache read-through (hit = no server fetch; miss = `transport.get` + populate cache within budget),
  materialize, drop the placeholder, refresh the index. **Refuses to overwrite an existing file** (a
  reappeared file wins; fail loud, never clobber).
- [ ] CLI: `sync hydrate <dir> [<path>...]` (default: all placeholders); README + milestone-plan doc
  updates.
**Test-first order (RED → GREEN):** extend `flow_sync_footprint.rs` —
4. `footprint_bounded_while_tree_grows` (**the M2 capability gate**): tree larger than the budget →
   backup → evict to fit → local bytes ≤ budget while the keep-set covers the whole tree → hydrate one
   file → byte-identical (content + mode + mtime).
5. `cache_hit_hydrate_fetches_nothing` (a counting transport wrapper): evict with cache spill → hydrate
   → zero `get` calls reach the server (the metered-egress win, observable).
6. `eviction_never_loses_data`: evict, wipe the cache entirely → hydrate refetches from the server and
   verifies (M1's tamper guard inherited via the shared materializer).
7. `hydrate_refuses_overwrite`: place a new file at an evicted path → hydrate refuses; the file is
   untouched; backup prefers the on-disk file and drops the placeholder.
**Done when:** the full flow suite green; behavioral: a directory whose logical size exceeds local disk
budget round-trips through evict → status → hydrate with every byte verified.
**Validation:** Moderate — flow + unit + a live drill: real server, evict a big file, `sync hydrate`,
`diff`; then wipe the cache and hydrate again (server path). Mutation audit: `cache.rs` +
`placeholder.rs` survivors triaged.

## Open Questions — resolved by default (user delegated execution 2026-08-07; overrides welcome)

- **Placeholder representation** — RESOLVED: absent file + state-DB record (stubs masquerade; see
  Reasoning). *ADVISORY.*
- **State root location** — RESOLVED: `$XDG_DATA_HOME/ciss-ctl/sync/<tree-id>/` (mirrors config.rs's
  XDG resolution), `--state-dir` override. *ADVISORY.*
- **Cache budget default** — RESOLVED: 256 MiB, persisted in state config, `--cache-budget` to change.
  *ADVISORY.*
- **Pin policy scope** — RESOLVED: the pin *mechanism* (bit + never-evict) ships; recent/starred/
  working-set *policies* deferred to M3+ where the working set becomes observable. *ADVISORY.*

## Review Log

- **2026-08-07 (abbreviated passes, one context)** — Pass 1: plan authored from the milestone M2 slice on
  shipped M1 ground. Pass 2 checks folded in: placeholder-merge is in `backup.rs` (not a wrapper) so every
  caller inherits it; evict requires *both* have-set and keep-set membership; the cache verifies on read
  (fail-safe); hydrate shares restore's materializer (single verified-write path); state root outside the
  tree (M1 learning). Pass 3 gates: every guard named RED-first above (no-data-loss, refuse-unbacked,
  budget/LRU, corrupt-cache-is-miss, refuse-overwrite, cache-hit-zero-fetch); tracing spec'd per flow;
  validation calibrated (narrow/moderate/moderate); concurrency map all-sequential; docs scheduled in the
  phases that stale them; mutation target `cache.rs`+`placeholder.rs`.

Eviction drops a file's local bytes only when every current chunk is
provably backed (server have-set AND committed keep-set — else refused
with the unbacked cids named); chunks spill into the budgeted cache,
the placeholder is recorded, then the file is deleted — in that order.
backup now commits the logical tree = scanned files ∪ placeholders

a reappeared file wins over its placeholder), takes SyncState instead
of a bare Index, and can re-upload an evicted file's chunks from the
cache if the server ever loses them (fail loud when neither side has
the bytes). CLI: sync evict/status; sync backup wires the per-tree
state root by default (--state-dir/--no-state; --no-state refuses when
placeholders exist).

TDD RED-first: backup_preserves_evicted_entries (identical fs-manifest
cid across an eviction), evict_refuses_unbacked_file (never-backed +
modified-since-backup), evicted_file_restores_cleanly. Live drill:
evict 1.8MB (6 chunks cached), status accurate, re-backup 0 uploads,
du byte-identical.

---
name: ciss-ctl-client-shipped
description: "ciss-ctl client CLI — where it lives, how it's released (in-repo crate + separate homebrew tap)"

---

`ciss-ctl` is the CISS client CLI, an in-repo workspace crate at
**`crates/ciss-cli`** (lib+bin; links the server's own crates so client crypto
can't drift). Capabilities: `key gen/import/show/list`, `login` (bsky app-password
→ `pds.json` 0600), `whoami`, `put`/`get` (default `--via pds`, `--via s3` opt-in,
one digest), `meter`, `ls`, `du` (self-only), `acl set/get` (gated reads Model
A/C), `--identity id|did`, `--json`, `-v`, hidden `man`. Plan + full per-phase
record: `docs/plans/2026-08-06-ciss-ctl-client-cli.md`. User docs: `docs/CLIENT.md`
+ `docs/CLIENT-TESTING.md` (both-sides guide vs the VPS).

**Distribution:** Homebrew tap **`CroftCommunity/homebrew-tap`** (cloned at
`/Users/cpettet/git/chasemp/CroftC/homebrew-tap`), formula `Formula/ciss-ctl.rb`.
`brew install croftcommunity/tap/ciss-ctl`. The formula builds `crates/ciss-cli`
from a **pinned release source tarball** (`url` + verified `sha256`), with a
retained `head` stanza and a man-page install.

**Release flow per change** (both repos use `chasemp`/github-personal; `gh auth
switch --user chasemp` — the account defaults to the Life360 EMU which 403s PR
creation): bump `version` in root `Cargo.toml` + `crates/ciss-cli/Cargo.toml`
(both, in lockstep) → PR+merge to CISS `main` → `git tag vX.Y.Z` + `gh release
create` with a `git archive --prefix=ciss-X.Y.Z/` tarball → **verify the
downloaded asset's sha256** → tap PR bumping `url`+`sha256` → **force-refresh the
brew tap clone** (`git -C "$(brew --repository croftcommunity/tap)" fetch origin
main && reset --hard origin/main` — `brew tap` re-clone goes stale) → `brew
upgrade`. Shipped through v0.5.6 as of 2026-08-06. See [[ciss-do-not-run-cargo-fmt]]
and [[ciss-no-cross-user-inspection-over-wire]].

All three work items are done. **PR #16 (M2) merged — `main` is at `9aa4adb`, tree clean, and it went through the new CI gate green.**

## What landed this session's final leg

**1. Discovery housekeeping** (`82037c8`, local commit in the discovery repo, unpushed like its neighbors): E90 stamped **M1 SHIPPED 2026-08-07** with the CISS PR reference, the "bsky app-token" auth line reconciled in place (the write path structurally needs the namespace key; the app-token path is read-side), and COHESION §67 got a status paragraph covering the shipped M1 plus the foundations-review deviations.

**2. CI gate** (PR #15, merged): `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the repo's two local gate commands (`cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace -- -D warnings`, deliberately no `cargo fmt`) on every PR and push to `main`, with `workflow_dispatch`, per-ref concurrency, a 30-minute timeout, and the toolchain pinned at 1.97.1 in `rust-toolchain.toml` resolved via rustup. Per the pattern's own instruction, I **proved the gate bites**: a deliberate failing test went red at exactly the `cargo test` step before being reverted. Note for the audit table in `CI-PATTERN.md`: CISS now satisfies the rules (I didn't edit that file — it's meta-repo content; happy to on request).

**3. M2 — bounded local footprint** (PR #16, merged, gated): three TDD phases on the M1 spine —
- **`sync evict`** refuses unless every chunk is provably backed (have-set *and* keep-set, unbacked cids named), spills chunks to a budgeted verify-on-read LRU cache, then drops the bytes.
- **The no-data-loss invariant** is the load-bearing piece: `backup` commits scanned files ∪ placeholders, proven by the flow test showing an *identical fs-manifest cid* across an eviction — plus a cache-recovery path if the server ever loses an evicted file's chunks, and `--no-state` refusing when placeholders exist.
- **`sync hydrate`** reads through the cache (a counting transport proved zero metered fetches on a hit) or verifies from the server, through the same materializer `restore` uses. Live drills: 6/6 chunks from cache, then 6/6 from the server after a cache wipe — byte-identical both ways.
- Gates: 55 suites green, clippy-pedantic 0, cargo-mutants on cache+placeholder 41 caught / 0 missed.

**Postponed as asked:** the tap release (noted in memory so a future session picks it up — the release flow with the version-lockstep and sha256 verification steps is recorded there).

**What's next on the ladder:** **M3 — two-device converge** — the multi-writer frontier made real: `DeviceHead` + `Frontier{heads}`, the client-side fold with conflict-copy, and the ladder's single server change (the additive owner-signed `Manifest.heads` field under I5). It's the milestone the whole spine was built for, and the first one that touches CISS itself — worth its own full phase-plan session.

# CISS file-sync — M3 execution plan (two-device converge, the frontier made real)

date: 2026-08-07
status: **Planned (condensed passes; the server phase is security-relevant and reasoned in full). EXECUTING.**
parent: `docs/plans/2026-08-07-file-sync-client.md` (milestone ladder; this doc executes **M3**).

## Problem Statement

Deliver **M3**: *"a second device converges, and a real conflict is preserved, not lost."* The
multi-writer frontier — per-device signed `DeviceHead`s named in a `Frontier.heads` map, folded
client-side — becomes real. This is the ladder's **only server change**: one additive, owner-signed
`heads` field on the CISS `Manifest`, bound into the signing preimage, still governed by I5. The server
gains no authority: it validates the signature and seq-monotonicity and stores bytes; the fold stays
entirely client-side; HEAD is never asserted or server-minted.

## Reasoning

**Why the server change is safe and small.** `heads: Option<BTreeMap<device_id, cid>>` on `Manifest`,
absent for every existing manifest. The signing preimage stays byte-identical when `heads` is `None`
(legacy manifests keep verifying — the back-compat guard is a RED-first test) and appends a canonical
heads digest when present, so a tampered or injected `heads` entry fails `verify()` exactly like a
tampered root (B1 extended, SECURITY-POSTURE updated in the same phase). I5 is untouched: a stale-seq
write is refused regardless of what its `heads` says, so a lagging device can never roll back another
device's head.

**The M3 no-data-loss invariant: the keep-set covers every head, not just mine.** A device committing
the Frontier commits the keep-set too — if it listed only its own tree, its commit would GC the *other*
device's chunks. So the commit computes keep-set = ∪ over **all** heads in the frontier being written:
each head's DeviceHead blob + fs-manifest + all its chunks + its base fs-manifest (manifest blob only —
the fold compares chunk *refs* against the base, never fetches base bytes). This lands RED-first, like
M2's placeholder-merge guard.

**Non-lossy concurrency by slot discipline.** Each device writes only `heads[its own device_id]`; a
stale-seq refusal (I5) triggers re-GET → re-apply own slot onto the fresh heads → retry (bounded).
Two devices committing concurrently both land; neither's head is ever overwritten by the other's retry.

**The fold is deterministic and clock-free.** Per-path 3-way merge against the last converged base
(client-local; each device records the folded tree's manifest cid as `base` after converging):
one-sided change → take it; identical → converged; divergent → **conflict-copy** (winner of the path by
content-address order — the smaller entry digest keeps the path, the loser materializes at
`<path>.conflict-<device_id>`; both contents preserved, both committed); modify-vs-delete → keep the
modification (non-lossy default, recorded here). mtime never participates (E90: timestamps are an
assertion). `DeviceHead` is a signed DAG-CBOR blob with a `croft.device-head/v1` kind self-tag (the
fs-manifest pattern), verified client-side on every fold — a head that fails its signature or tag is
rejected even from "yourself" (the corpus's HEAD doctrine).

**Rename detection: deliberately skipped (⏭️).** Dedup already gives the prize — a rename is
delete+add whose chunks the server has, so **zero chunks transfer** without any detection (tested as
such). Exact-chunk-set detection remains the recorded optional polish.

**Device identity (shared-key era):** `device_id` = a stable self-asserted install label, generated
once per profile (random 8-hex, stored in the profile config dir); `counter`/`parent` (the per-device
chain) live in the per-tree SyncState.

## Verified Assumptions

- `signing_preimage` = `ciss/v1/manifest:signer:seq:leaf_count:total_bytes:root` (src/manifest.rs:115);
  `Manifest` + `ManifestLeaf` are `deny_unknown_fields` (so `heads` needs `#[serde(default)]` +
  skip-if-none to keep old-wire compatibility); `verify()` checks leaves/root/total then the signature
  (src/manifest.rs:168). `build_manifest` is pre-1.0 — signature change, call sites updated, no compat
  shims (CLAUDE.md).
- Server manifest tests live in `tests/e2_manifest.rs` (+ `wiring_*`/flow guards); the M1/M2 client
  stack (`HttpCiss`, `SyncState`, materializer, flow harness) is on main.

## Documentation Impact

- `docs/SECURITY-POSTURE.md` — B1 wording: the manifest signature also binds `heads` when present. **Phase 1.**
- `README.md` — `sync converge` line. **Phase 3.**
- `docs/plans/2026-08-07-file-sync-client.md` — M3 stamp + the one-server-change note marked done. **Phase 3.**

## Concurrency Map

**All phases sequential** (Phase 2 needs Phase 1's wire field; Phase 3 needs Phase 2's commit loop).

## Phases

### Phase 1: CISS server — additive owner-signed `Manifest.heads` under I5
**Changes:** `heads: Option<BTreeMap<String, String>>` on `Manifest` (`default` + skip-if-none);
preimage appends `:heads=<sha256 over "id=cid;"… sorted>` **only when present**; `build_manifest` gains
the heads param (call sites updated); `verify()` covers it via the preimage; server handlers unchanged
(self-authorizing PUT already verifies). POSTURE B1 note.
**Test-first (RED):** `legacy_manifest_without_heads_still_verifies` (byte-identical preimage — the
back-compat guard); `tampered_heads_fails_verify` (add/remove/alter an entry after signing);
`heads_round_trips_over_the_wire` (PUT with heads → GET returns them, second session reads them);
`stale_seq_with_different_heads_refused` (I5 holds; the stored heads unchanged).
**Validation:** server-side unit + wiring; this is a signing-surface change → mutation audit on
`src/manifest.rs` after green.

### Phase 2: engine — `DeviceHead` + the non-lossy frontier commit
**Changes:** `device_head.rs` (record + kind tag + sign/verify over a domain-tagged preimage);
`SyncState` gains `device_id()` (profile-level, generated once), `counter`/`last_head`/`base` columns;
`backup` becomes frontier-aware behind the same API: upload DeviceHead blob, keep-set = ∪ all heads'
closures (the invariant above), commit `heads[my_id]` with bounded stale-seq retry re-applying only the
own slot.
**Test-first (RED):** flow `tests/flow_sync_frontier.rs` — `two_devices_both_land` (B commits between
A's read and write; A's retry lands; both heads present; **neither device's chunks left the keep-set**);
`keep_set_covers_other_head` (the no-data-loss guard, distinct assert); `device_head_chain`
(counter/parent advance; a bad signature or wrong kind is rejected on read).

### Phase 3: engine + CLI — the fold, conflict-copy, `sync converge`
**Changes:** `fold.rs` (3-way per-path vs base; the decision table above; deterministic conflict
naming); `converge` flow (fetch heads' manifests → fold → materialize deltas via the shared
materializer → commit folded tree as own head → record new base); CLI `sync converge <dir>`; docs.
**Test-first (RED):** `disjoint_edits_merge` (A adds x, B edits y → both trees identical afterward,
content_ids equal); `same_path_divergence_preserved` (both edit p → winner at p by content-address,
loser at `p.conflict-<id>`, both byte-contents present on **both** devices after each converges);
`rename_transfers_zero_chunks` (mv a→b on A; B converges; report shows 0 uploaded/0 fetched-from-server
for content, dedup carries it); `modify_beats_delete` (recorded default).
**Validation:** moderate+ — flow suite + a live two-device drill against a real server (two state
roots/profiles, real conflict, verify both converge byte-identically).

## Open Questions — resolved by default (execution delegated; overrides welcome)

- Conflict naming `<path>.conflict-<device_id>` with content-address winner-keeps-path. *ADVISORY.*
- Modify-vs-delete → modification wins (non-lossy). *ADVISORY.*
- Rename detection skipped (dedup already zero-transfer). *ADVISORY, recorded ⏭️.*
- Frontier `base` = client-local last-converged manifest cid (not a server object). *ADVISORY.*

## Review Log

- **2026-08-07 (condensed passes)** — plan authored from the milestone M3 slice + the settled frontier
  design. Pass-2/3 checks folded in: preimage back-compat guard named RED-first; keep-set-covers-all-heads
  as the phase-2 centerpiece; fold decision table written down before code; server phase carries the
  POSTURE doc update in-phase; mutation audit scoped to `manifest.rs` (signing surface) + `fold.rs`.

2	
3	date: 2026-08-07
4	status: **CLOSED (2026-08-07). All three phases shipped; M3 delivered:** *a second device converges,
5	and a real conflict is preserved, not lost* — `ciss-ctl sync converge`, the frontier real.
6	
7	## Outcome Summary
8	
9	| Phase | Outcome | Commit | Note |
10	|---|---|---|---|
11	| 1 server `heads` field | ✅ | `a1b2673` | preimage-bound, back-compat proven; manifest mutants: survivor closed, 0 missed |

14	parent: `docs/plans/2026-08-07-file-sync-client.md` (milestone ladder; this doc executes **M3**).
15	
16	## Problem Statement
17	
18	Deliver **M3**: *"a second device converges, and a real conflict is preserved, not lost."* The
19	multi-writer frontier — per-device signed `DeviceHead`s named in a `Frontier.heads` map, folded
20	client-side — becomes real. This is the ladder's **only server change**: one additive, owner-signed
21	`heads` field on the CISS `Manifest`, bound into the signing preimage, still governed by I5. The server
22	gains no authority: it validates the signature and seq-monotonicity and stores bytes; the fold stays
23	entirely client-side; HEAD is never asserted or server-minted.
24	
25	## Reasoning
26	
27	**Why the server change is safe and small.** `heads: Option<BTreeMap<device_id, cid>>` on `Manifest`,
28	absent for every existing manifest. The signing preimage stays byte-identical when `heads` is `None`
29	(legacy manifests keep verifying — the back-compat guard is a RED-first test) and appends a canonical
30	heads digest when present, so a tampered or injected `heads` entry fails `verify()` exactly like a
31	tampered root (B1 extended, SECURITY-POSTURE updated in the same phase). I5 is untouched: a stale-seq
32	write is refused regardless of what its `heads` says, so a lagging device can never roll back another
33	device's head.
34	
35	**The M3 no-data-loss invariant: the keep-set covers every head, not just mine.** A device committing
36	the Frontier commits the keep-set too — if it listed only its own tree, its commit would GC the *other*
37	device's chunks. So the commit computes keep-set = ∪ over **all** heads in the frontier being written:
38	each head's DeviceHead blob + fs-manifest + all its chunks + its base fs-manifest (manifest blob only —
39	the fold compares chunk *refs* against the base, never fetches base bytes). This lands RED-first, like
40	M2's placeholder-merge guard.
41	
42	**Non-lossy concurrency by slot discipline.** Each device writes only `heads[its own device_id]`; a
43	stale-seq refusal (I5) triggers re-GET → re-apply own slot onto the fresh heads → retry (bounded).
44	Two devices committing concurrently both land; neither's head is ever overwritten by the other's retry.
45	
46	**The fold is deterministic and clock-free.** Per-path 3-way merge against the last converged base
47	(client-local; each device records the folded tree's manifest cid as `base` after converging):
48	one-sided change → take it; identical → converged; divergent → **conflict-copy** (winner of the path by
49	content-address order — the smaller entry digest keeps the path, the loser materializes at
50	`<path>.conflict-<device_id>`; both contents preserved, both committed); modify-vs-delete → keep the
51	modification (non-lossy default, recorded here). mtime never participates (E90: timestamps are an
52	assertion). `DeviceHead` is a signed DAG-CBOR blob with a `croft.device-head/v1` kind self-tag (the
53	fs-manifest pattern), verified client-side on every fold — a head that fails its signature or tag is
54	rejected even from "yourself" (the corpus's HEAD doctrine).
55	
56	**Rename detection: deliberately skipped (⏭️).** Dedup already gives the prize — a rename is
57	delete+add whose chunks the server has, so **zero chunks transfer** without any detection (tested as
58	such). Exact-chunk-set detection remains the recorded optional polish.
59	
60	**Device identity (shared-key era):** `device_id` = a stable self-asserted install label, generated
61	once per profile (random 8-hex, stored in the profile config dir); `counter`/`parent` (the per-device
62	chain) live in the per-tree SyncState.
63	
64	## Verified Assumptions
65	
66	- `signing_preimage` = `ciss/v1/manifest:signer:seq:leaf_count:total_bytes:root` (src/manifest.rs:115);
67	  `Manifest` + `ManifestLeaf` are `deny_unknown_fields` (so `heads` needs `#[serde(default)]` +
68	  skip-if-none to keep old-wire compatibility); `verify()` checks leaves/root/total then the signature
69	  (src/manifest.rs:168). `build_manifest` is pre-1.0 — signature change, call sites updated, no compat
70	  shims (CLAUDE.md).
71	- Server manifest tests live in `tests/e2_manifest.rs` (+ `wiring_*`/flow guards); the M1/M2 client
72	  stack (`HttpCiss`, `SyncState`, materializer, flow harness) is on main.
73	
74	## Documentation Impact
75	
76	- `docs/SECURITY-POSTURE.md` — B1 wording: the manifest signature also binds `heads` when present. **Phase 1.**
77	- `README.md` — `sync converge` line. **Phase 3.**
78	- `docs/plans/2026-08-07-file-sync-client.md` — M3 stamp + the one-server-change note marked done. **Phase 3.**
79	
80	## Concurrency Map
81	
82	**All phases sequential** (Phase 2 needs Phase 1's wire field; Phase 3 needs Phase 2's commit loop).
83	
84	## Phases
85	
86	### Phase 1: CISS server — additive owner-signed `Manifest.heads` under I5 — ✅ SHIPPED (`a1b2673`)
87	**Changes:** `heads: Option<BTreeMap<String, String>>` on `Manifest` (`default` + skip-if-none);
88	preimage appends `:heads=<sha256 over "id=cid;"… sorted>` **only when present**; `build_manifest` gains
89	the heads param (call sites updated); `verify()` covers it via the preimage; server handlers unchanged

content.text:
**M3 is merged — the multi-writer frontier is real.** `main` is at `6f58174`, tree clean, all three M3 phases through the CI gate.

## What M3 delivered (PR #17)

This was the milestone the whole spine existed for — the first concrete instance of the corpus's parked frontier machinery, and the ladder's only server change:

- **The server change** (`a1b2673`): `Manifest.heads` — owner-signed via a canonical digest appended to the signing preimage, so a head can't be altered, injected, or stripped after signing. Back-compat is *structural*: absent heads = the byte-identical legacy preimage, so every pre-frontier manifest still verifies (proven RED-first). The server gained zero authority — it still just checks the signature and seq and stores bytes. POSTURE B1 updated in-phase.
- **The non-lossy commit** (`9e8c8c5`): self-verifying `DeviceHead` records (every field signature-bound; forgeries rejected even "from yourself"), slot discipline (write only your own `heads` entry), bounded stale-seq retry, and the keep-set covering *every* head's closure so one device's commit can never orphan another's bytes. The flow test injects device B's entire backup between A's frontier read and first commit — A retries exactly once and both heads land.
- **The fold** (`e4c5a98`): pure, deterministic, clock-free. In the live drill, two profiles sharing the account key with a same-path conflict each ran `sync converge` and landed on the **same fs-manifest cid**, `diff -r` byte-identical, with both conflicting contents preserved on both devices. The self-healing property fell out of the algebra: B's converge re-derives A's fold exactly, no coordination round needed.

Audits: manifest mutants 0 missed (including a real pre-existing gap the audit exposed — nothing had ever asserted different leaf sets produce different Merkle roots); fold mutants 9/0 after pinning the conflict tiebreak to the digest rather than device-name order.

## Where the ladder stands

M1 ✅ → M2 ✅ → **M3 ✅** → M4 (iroh peer-fetch) → M5 (cost twin). Discovery's E90 is stamped M1–M3 (`264e016`, local), memory updated.

**My recommendation for what's next:** M4 in a fresh session. It's the first milestone with genuinely new territory — the iroh dependency stack (iroh-blobs 0.102, Bao verified streaming, gossip bootstrap) — which deserves a real Phase-0 discovery with probes rather than riding this session's tail. The blake3 half of every `ChunkRef` has been waiting for it since M1. M5 is smaller and could ride afterward; its embryo (the pre-transfer pricing line) is already logging. And the postponed tap release is still queued whenever you want `sync` on the deployed box.

`ciss-ctl` is the CISS client CLI, an in-repo workspace crate at
**`crates/ciss-cli`** (lib+bin; links the server's own crates so client crypto
can't drift). Capabilities: `key gen/import/show/list`, `login` (bsky app-password
→ `pds.json` 0600), `whoami`, `put`/`get` (default `--via pds`, `--via s3` opt-in,
one digest), `meter`, `ls`, `du` (self-only), `acl set/get` (gated reads Model
A/C), `--identity id|did`, `--json`, `-v`, hidden `man`. Plan + full per-phase
record: `docs/plans/2026-08-06-ciss-ctl-client-cli.md`. User docs: `docs/CLIENT.md`
+ `docs/CLIENT-TESTING.md` (both-sides guide vs the VPS).

**File-sync (2026-08-07, M1+M2+M3 merged to main, NOT yet released to the tap):**
`sync backup|restore|evict|hydrate|status|converge` over the new `crates/ciss-sync`
engine (FastCDC dual sha256/blake3 chunks, DAG-CBOR fs-manifest, keep-set under I5,
per-tree state root in `$XDG_DATA_HOME/ciss-ctl/sync/`). M3 shipped the frontier:
`Manifest.heads` (owner-signed, preimage-bound, back-compat structural — the
ladder's only server change), self-verifying `DeviceHead`s, and the deterministic
clock-free fold with conflict-copies. Multi-device backup uses a per-profile
`device_id` file; two devices sharing the account key converge to identical trees.
`id:` plane only. Plans: `docs/plans/2026-08-07-file-sync-*.md`. CI gate live
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, toolchain pinned 1.97.1). Remaining ladder: M4 (iroh
peer-fetch — needs a real Phase-0 discovery for iroh-blobs 0.102 APIs) and M5
(cost twin — the pre-transfer pricing INFO line is its embryo). A tap release
including `sync` is the postponed next release step.

**Distribution:** Homebrew tap **`CroftCommunity/homebrew-tap`** (cloned at
`/Users/cpettet/git/chasemp/CroftC/homebrew-tap`), formula `Formula/ciss-ctl.rb`.
`brew install croftcommunity/tap/ciss-ctl`. The formula builds `crates/ciss-cli`
from a **pinned release source tarball** (`url` + verified `sha256`), with a
retained `head` stanza and a man-page install.

**Release flow per change** (both repos use `chasemp`/github-personal; `gh auth
switch --user chasemp` — the account defaults to the Life360 EMU which 403s PR
creation): bump `version` in root `Cargo.toml` + `crates/ciss-cli/Cargo.toml`
(both, in lockstep) → PR+merge to CISS `main` → `git tag vX.Y.Z` + `gh release
create` with a `git archive --prefix=ciss-X.Y.Z/` tarball → **verify the
downloaded asset's sha256** → tap PR bumping `url`+`sha256` → **force-refresh the
brew tap clone** (`git -C "$(brew --repository croftcommunity/tap)" fetch origin
main && reset --hard origin/main` — `brew tap` re-clone goes stale) → `brew
upgrade`. Shipped through v0.5.6 as of 2026-08-06. See [[ciss-do-not-run-cargo-fmt]]
and [[ciss-no-cross-user-inspection-over-wire]].

### 10.1 The key-hierarchy fork — DECIDED 2026-06-16: (a) live + (b) backup-only

**Decision:** logical binding (a) for the live path, with an optional HD seed (b) reserved
*purely* as a lose-all-devices backup. The live path never uses derivation; the seed is not in
the normal-operation threat surface. This keeps "keys are not identity" for everything that
runs day-to-day, and gives the recovery gate (G1) a concrete anchor without making a single
seed the crown jewel of live operation. It mirrors the COHESION #12 framing ("delegation
primary + optional trust-minimized backup").

# iroh 1.0.0 API — verified against source (not guessed)

Per the "verify against source, never guess" rule. Every symbol below was read from the pinned
1.0.0 source extracted under `.node4-cargo/registry/src/.../{iroh,iroh-relay,iroh-base}-1.0.0`.
Citations are `crate/path:line`. This is the surface the E0 harness is built on.

## Client endpoint (generator)

- `Endpoint::builder(preset: impl Preset) -> Builder` — `iroh/src/endpoint.rs:940`.
- Presets — `iroh/src/endpoint/presets.rs`: `Empty` (sets nothing), `Minimal` (crypto provider only;
  needs `tls-ring`/`tls-aws-lc-rs` — in default features), `N0` (full n0 DNS+relays). **Lab uses
  `presets::Minimal`** + explicit relay/bind.
- Builder: `.secret_key(SecretKey)` `:524`, `.alpns(Vec<Vec<u8>>)` `:535`,
  `.bind_addr(A)` `:363`, `.relay_mode(RelayMode)` `:557`, `.ca_tls_config(CaTlsConfig)` `:713`,
  `.bind().await -> Endpoint`.
- `RelayMode::Custom(RelayMap)` / `RelayMode::custom(impl IntoIterator<Item=RelayUrl>)` — `:1950`.
- `endpoint.online().await` `:1345`, `endpoint.addr() -> EndpointAddr` `:1186`.
- `endpoint.connect(impl Into<EndpointAddr>, alpn: &[u8]).await -> Result<Connection, ConnectError>`
  — `:1040`.

## Forced relay-only passthrough (E0 worst case)

- `EndpointAddr::from_parts(id: PublicKey, addrs: impl IntoIterator<Item=TransportAddr>)` —
  `iroh-base/src/endpoint_addr.rs:104`.
- `TransportAddr::Relay(RelayUrl)` — `:57`; `.is_relay()` `:67`. A relay-only addr =
  `from_parts(peer_id, [TransportAddr::Relay(url)])` — no direct IPs ⇒ relay path only.

## Path detection (the core E0 metric)

- `conn.paths() -> PathList` — `iroh/src/endpoint/connection.rs:1095` (snapshot at call time).
- `PathList::iter() -> PathListIter` over `Path`.
- `Path` — `iroh/src/socket/remote_map/remote_state/path_watcher.rs:453`:
  `.is_selected() -> bool` `:470` (the live path), `.is_relay() -> bool` `:480`,
  `.is_ip() -> bool` `:475`, `.rtt() -> Duration` `:494`, `.stats() -> PathStats` `:489`,
  `.remote_addr() -> &TransportAddr` `:460`.
- **Live-path classification:** `conn.paths().iter().find(|p| p.is_selected())` then `.is_relay()` +
  `.rtt()`. (`conn.paths().iter().any(|p| p.is_relay())` per spec also works for "is a relay path open".)
- `conn.paths_stream()` `:1108` / `conn.path_events()` `:1127` to watch matchmaking flip relay→direct.

## Relay server (E0 single relay)

- `iroh_relay::server::RelayConfig::new((ip, port))` — `iroh-relay/src/server.rs:150` (server config;
  alias as `RelayServerConfig`). Fields: `.tls: Option<TlsConfig>` (None ⇒ plain HTTP), `.access:
  Arc<dyn DynAccessControl>`, `.key_cache_capacity`.
- Self-signed certs: `iroh_relay::server::testing::self_signed_tls_certs_and_config() ->
  (Vec<CertificateDer>, rustls::ServerConfig)` — `iroh-relay/src/server/testing.rs:9` (SANs:
  localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1).
- `TlsConfig::new((ip,0), CertConfig::Manual { server_config })`.
- `ServerConfig::default()` then `.relay = Some(relay)`, `.quic = Some(QuicConfig::new((ip,0)))`.
- `Server::spawn(ServerConfig).await -> Result<Server, SpawnError>` — `:691`; `server.https_addr()`,
  `server.quic_addr()`.
- Client relay map: `RelayMap = iroh::RelayConfig::new(url: RelayUrl, Option<RelayQuicConfig>).into()`
  — `iroh-relay/src/relay_map.rs:250`; `RelayQuicConfig::new(port)` `:299`.

## Admit hook (E3; E0 baseline uses AllowAll)

- `trait AccessControl { async fn on_connect(&self, &ClientRequest) -> Access }` —
  `iroh-relay/src/server.rs:285`; `AllowAll` `:340`.
- `enum Access { Allow, Deny { reason: Option<String> } }` — `:350`.

## Lab TLS posture (⚠️ LAB-ONLY)

Self-signed relay cert SANs are localhost/127.0.0.1/::1; cross-VPC relay URLs use box IPs, so client
cert verification would fail. The lab uses `CaTlsConfig::insecure_skip_verify()`
(`iroh-relay/src/tls.rs:94`, gated behind `test-utils`) on the generator endpoints.
⚠️ WARNING: insecure_skip_verify disables relay-server cert verification — acceptable only because
this is a closed sandbox VPC measuring relay capacity over iroh's own encrypted layer; never ship it.
Alternative for a hardened run: `CaTlsConfig::custom_roots([cert_der])` + a relay URL whose host is in
the cert SANs.

## Deferred-to-controller (E2) — not yet verified, flagged for task 6

`DnsAddressLookup::builder(origin)`, the in-memory/static address lookup + `add_endpoint_info`
(rc.1 `MemoryLookup` → 1.0 name TBD), `PkarrPublisher`. Verify against source before building ctrl/.

input.content:
# M4 — iroh peer-fetch: the same sync runs over iroh, and blobs can come from a peer

**Status:** IN PROGRESS
**Parent plan:** `docs/plans/2026-08-07-file-sync-client.md` (M4 section)
**Server change:** none — CISS becomes one blob source among peers.

## Problem Statement

M1–M3 built a complete own-device sync (chunk → backup/restore → bounded
footprint → two-device converge), but every byte moves through CISS: all reads
are metered origin egress, and a device pair on the same LAN still round-trips
the server. Every `ChunkRef` has carried a blake3 hash since M1 *for exactly
this milestone* — the engine was designed so a peer-to-peer, blake3-addressed
transport could slot in under the same `BlobTransport`/`ManifestSlot` seams
without touching the engine or the server. M4 cashes that in: blobs can be
fetched from a peer device (Bao-verified streaming), and the whole converge
flow can run device↔device over iroh-gossip with the server offline.

## Approach

Two phases behind the existing seams; zero engine-semantics change; zero server
change.

1. **P1 — `IrohPeer`: `BlobTransport` over iroh-blobs, plus `PeerFirst`
   fallback.** New workspace crate `crates/ciss-iroh` (mirrors the HttpCiss
   placement rule: transport impls live outside the engine). `IrohPeer` keys by
   the canonical sha-256 cid (C1 stays the address of record) and maintains an
   internal sha256→(blake3, providers) index; bytes live in an iroh-blobs
   `MemStore` served via `BlobsProtocol` behind a `Router`. `get` resolves the
   blake3, downloads from a provider if local-missing (Bao verifies blake3 in
   transit), then **re-verifies sha-256 on receipt** — C1 enforcement is not
   delegated to iroh. `PeerFirst` composes `IrohPeer` over an origin
   `BlobTransport`: `get` tries the peer, falls back to origin per blob
   (including on integrity mismatch — a poisoned sha256→blake3 mapping degrades
   to an origin fetch, never to wrong bytes); `put`/`have` delegate to origin
   (the keep-set and billing semantics of backup are unchanged).

2. **P2 — serverless converge over iroh-gossip.** `IrohPeer` additionally
   implements `ManifestSlot` + `AccountKey`, making `converge()` run unchanged
   with no server: `frontier()` is the union-by-device of gossip head
   announcements (per-device newest `counter` wins — each device only ever
   writes its own slot, so no cross-device CAS is needed; `DeviceHead` records
   stay self-verifying exactly as in M3); `commit_frontier` records own heads
   locally and broadcasts an announcement. The announcement carries only two
   hash-pairs — `(head_cid_sha256, head_blake3)` and `(fs_root_sha256,
   fs_root_blake3)` — everything else is derivable: fetch the head, decode
   (signature-verified), fetch the fs-manifest, and every `ChunkRef` inside it
   populates the sha256→blake3 index. Topic = `sha256("croft.sync-topic/v1:" +
   account_pubkey_z32)` — both devices derive it independently
   (`discovery/alpha/thinking/multi-device.md` §10: TopicId = derive(lineage
   root); the lineage root today is the shared account key). CLI:
   `ciss-ctl sync p2p share` (serve + announce; prints a base64 JSON ticket of
   the local `EndpointAddr`) and `ciss-ctl sync p2p converge --ticket <t>`.

## Reasoning

- **Why a new crate, not a feature in ciss-sync:** the iroh stack is heavy
  (~450 deps); the engine stays lean and its consumers (a future GUI, the meer)
  don't inherit iroh. Same dependency-direction logic that put `HttpCiss` in
  ciss-cli (M1 OQ1).
- **Why sha-256 stays the key:** C1 says the server names content by sha-256;
  the engine, manifests, and keep-set all speak it. blake3 is a transport-level
  alias carried since M1. Re-verifying sha-256 on every peer-served blob means
  a malicious/buggy peer (or poisoned mapping) can waste a fetch but never
  corrupt a tree — the same fail-closed posture as the M1 tamper guard.
- **Why union-by-device replaces the seq-CAS serverless:** I5's monotonic seq
  exists to serialize *shared-slot* writes on one server. Serverless, each
  device is the sole writer of its own head slot and `DeviceHead.counter`
  (signed) already gives per-writer ordering — union + newest-counter is the
  natural CRDT of that structure, and `converge`'s decode-verify step remains
  the integrity gate. No new trust is granted: same shared account key as M3.
- **Why LAN-first (no relay/discovery infra):** relay selection and n0/global
  discovery are deployment posture (croft-stack), not engine semantics. The
  ticket carries full direct addresses; `presets::Minimal` +
  `RelayMode::Disabled` keeps the probe-verified surface. Relay enablement is a
  flag away when wanted (out of scope, noted below).

## Phase 0 — discovery (DONE, probes in session scratchpad)

Pinned versions: **iroh 1.0.3, iroh-blobs 0.103.0, iroh-gossip 0.101.0**
(current patch releases of the FACTCHECK-registered 1.0.0/0.102/0.100 lines);
MSRV 1.91 ≤ pinned toolchain 1.97.1; probes built and ran on rustc 1.97.1.
Core endpoint surface was already source-verified in
`experiments/alpha/iroh/relay-lab-runs/IROH-1.0.0-API-VERIFIED.md`.

Verified by running probes (two endpoints, loopback, `RelayMode::Disabled`):

- `store.blobs().add_bytes(bytes)` → tag whose `hash` **is byte-identical to
  `blake3::hash(bytes)`** — every `ChunkRef.blake3` is directly the iroh
  address, no re-hash needed.
- Serve: `BlobsProtocol::new(&store, None)` +
  `Router::builder(ep).accept(iroh_blobs::ALPN, blobs).spawn()`.
- Fetch: `store.downloader(&endpoint).download(hash, Some(node_id)).await` with
  the provider's `EndpointAddr` registered in the fetcher's `MemoryLookup`;
  `blobs().has(hash)` / `get_bytes(hash)` for local checks. Fetched bytes
  byte-identical; sha-256 recomputation matches.
- Endpoint recipe: `Endpoint::builder(presets::Minimal)
  .address_lookup(MemoryLookup).relay_mode(RelayMode::Disabled)
  .bind_addr(127.0.0.1:0)` (`presets::Empty` fails: no rustls crypto provider).
- Gossip: `Gossip::builder().spawn(ep)` + accept `GOSSIP_ALPN`;
  `subscribe_and_join(topic, bootstrap_ids)` → `(GossipSender,
  GossipReceiver)`; `sender.broadcast(Bytes)` delivered as
  `Event::Received(msg)`, content intact; `TopicId::from_bytes([u8; 32])`
  accepts a sha-256 digest.

## Phases

### P1 — `IrohPeer` blob path + `PeerFirst` fallback

RED-first, in `crates/ciss-iroh` (crate tests use an in-memory origin mock —
no CISS `World` dependency inside the crate):

1. `IrohPeer` put→have→get local roundtrip, sha-256 keyed (put verifies the
   cid matches the bytes — same contract HttpCiss enforces).
2. Two `IrohPeer`s on loopback: A `put`s, B learns the mapping + provider,
   B `get`s → bytes identical, sha-256 verified.
3. A **poisoned mapping** (sha256 key → blake3 of different content) on `get`
   fails closed with a cid-naming error (crate level), and through `PeerFirst`
   degrades to an origin fetch with correct bytes (fallback level).
4. `PeerFirst`: `get` prefers peer, falls back per blob when the peer lacks
   it; `put`/`have`/`ManifestSlot`/`AccountKey` delegate to origin untouched.

Workflow tier (root `tests/flow_sync_peer_fetch.rs`, real `World` origin):
backup to CISS, seed a peer, restore via `PeerFirst` → tree byte-identical
AND the origin served strictly fewer blob gets than the blob count (peer-fetch
= less metered egress, observed not asserted-by-faith).

# M4 — iroh peer-fetch: the same sync runs over iroh, and blobs can come from a peer

**Status:** IN PROGRESS
**Parent plan:** `docs/plans/2026-08-07-file-sync-client.md` (M4 section)
**Server change:** none — CISS becomes one blob source among peers.

## Problem Statement

M1–M3 built a complete own-device sync (chunk → backup/restore → bounded
footprint → two-device converge), but every byte moves through CISS: all reads
are metered origin egress, and a device pair on the same LAN still round-trips
the server. Every `ChunkRef` has carried a blake3 hash since M1 *for exactly
this milestone* — the engine was designed so a peer-to-peer, blake3-addressed
transport could slot in under the same `BlobTransport`/`ManifestSlot` seams
without touching the engine or the server. M4 cashes that in: blobs can be
fetched from a peer device (Bao-verified streaming), and the whole converge
flow can run device↔device over iroh-gossip with the server offline.

## Approach

Two phases behind the existing seams; zero engine-semantics change; zero server
change.

1. **P1 — `IrohPeer`: `BlobTransport` over iroh-blobs, plus `PeerFirst`
   fallback.** New workspace crate `crates/ciss-iroh` (mirrors the HttpCiss
   placement rule: transport impls live outside the engine). `IrohPeer` keys by
   the canonical sha-256 cid (C1 stays the address of record) and maintains an
   internal sha256→(blake3, providers) index; bytes live in an iroh-blobs
   `MemStore` served via `BlobsProtocol` behind a `Router`. `get` resolves the
   blake3, downloads from a provider if local-missing (Bao verifies blake3 in
   transit), then **re-verifies sha-256 on receipt** — C1 enforcement is not
   delegated to iroh. `PeerFirst` composes `IrohPeer` over an origin
   `BlobTransport`: `get` tries the peer, falls back to origin per blob
   (including on integrity mismatch — a poisoned sha256→blake3 mapping degrades
   to an origin fetch, never to wrong bytes); `put`/`have` delegate to origin
   (the keep-set and billing semantics of backup are unchanged).

2. **P2 — serverless converge over iroh-gossip.** `IrohPeer` additionally
   implements `ManifestSlot` + `AccountKey`, making `converge()` run unchanged
   with no server: `frontier()` is the union-by-device of gossip head
   announcements (per-device newest `counter` wins — each device only ever
   writes its own slot, so no cross-device CAS is needed; `DeviceHead` records
   stay self-verifying exactly as in M3); `commit_frontier` records own heads
   locally and broadcasts an announcement. The announcement carries only two
   hash-pairs — `(head_cid_sha256, head_blake3)` and `(fs_root_sha256,
   fs_root_blake3)` — everything else is derivable: fetch the head, decode
   (signature-verified), fetch the fs-manifest, and every `ChunkRef` inside it
   populates the sha256→blake3 index. Topic = `sha256("croft.sync-topic/v1:" +
   account_pubkey_z32)` — both devices derive it independently
   (`discovery/alpha/thinking/multi-device.md` §10: TopicId = derive(lineage
   root); the lineage root today is the shared account key). CLI:
   `ciss-ctl sync p2p share` (serve + announce; prints a base64 JSON ticket of
   the local `EndpointAddr`) and `ciss-ctl sync p2p converge --ticket <t>`.

## Reasoning

- **Why a new crate, not a feature in ciss-sync:** the iroh stack is heavy
  (~450 deps); the engine stays lean and its consumers (a future GUI, the meer)
  don't inherit iroh. Same dependency-direction logic that put `HttpCiss` in
  ciss-cli (M1 OQ1).
- **Why sha-256 stays the key:** C1 says the server names content by sha-256;
  the engine, manifests, and keep-set all speak it. blake3 is a transport-level
  alias carried since M1. Re-verifying sha-256 on every peer-served blob means
  a malicious/buggy peer (or poisoned mapping) can waste a fetch but never
  corrupt a tree — the same fail-closed posture as the M1 tamper guard.
- **Why union-by-device replaces the seq-CAS serverless:** I5's monotonic seq
  exists to serialize *shared-slot* writes on one server. Serverless, each
  device is the sole writer of its own head slot and `DeviceHead.counter`
  (signed) already gives per-writer ordering — union + newest-counter is the
  natural CRDT of that structure, and `converge`'s decode-verify step remains
  the integrity gate. No new trust is granted: same shared account key as M3.
- **Why LAN-first (no relay/discovery infra):** relay selection and n0/global
  discovery are deployment posture (croft-stack), not engine semantics. The
  ticket carries full direct addresses; `presets::Minimal` +
  `RelayMode::Disabled` keeps the probe-verified surface. Relay enablement is a
  flag away when wanted (out of scope, noted below).

## Phase 0 — discovery (DONE, probes in session scratchpad)

Pinned versions: **iroh 1.0.3, iroh-blobs 0.103.0, iroh-gossip 0.101.0**
(current patch releases of the FACTCHECK-registered 1.0.0/0.102/0.100 lines);
MSRV 1.91 ≤ pinned toolchain 1.97.1; probes built and ran on rustc 1.97.1.
Core endpoint surface was already source-verified in
`experiments/alpha/iroh/relay-lab-runs/IROH-1.0.0-API-VERIFIED.md`.

Verified by running probes (two endpoints, loopback, `RelayMode::Disabled`):

- `store.blobs().add_bytes(bytes)` → tag whose `hash` **is byte-identical to
  `blake3::hash(bytes)`** — every `ChunkRef.blake3` is directly the iroh
  address, no re-hash needed.
- Serve: `BlobsProtocol::new(&store, None)` +
  `Router::builder(ep).accept(iroh_blobs::ALPN, blobs).spawn()`.
- Fetch: `store.downloader(&endpoint).download(hash, Some(node_id)).await` with
  the provider's `EndpointAddr` registered in the fetcher's `MemoryLookup`;
  `blobs().has(hash)` / `get_bytes(hash)` for local checks. Fetched bytes
  byte-identical; sha-256 recomputation matches.
- Endpoint recipe: `Endpoint::builder(presets::Minimal)
  .address_lookup(MemoryLookup).relay_mode(RelayMode::Disabled)
  .bind_addr(127.0.0.1:0)` (`presets::Empty` fails: no rustls crypto provider).
- Gossip: `Gossip::builder().spawn(ep)` + accept `GOSSIP_ALPN`;
  `subscribe_and_join(topic, bootstrap_ids)` → `(GossipSender,
  GossipReceiver)`; `sender.broadcast(Bytes)` delivered as

MeshPeer implements the engine's full transport surface (BlobTransport +
ManifestSlot + AccountKey) over iroh alone, so ciss_sync::converge runs
unchanged with no server. The frontier is the union of gossip head
announcements with newest-signed-counter-wins per device — each device is
the sole writer of its own slot, so no cross-device CAS is needed; the

multi-device.md §10 (TopicId = derive(lineage_root)). An announcement
carries only two hash-pairs; a fetched fs-manifest self-primes the
sha256→blake3 index for every chunk it references. Flow test: two devices
with disjoint + conflicting edits converge to the identical tree with the
server offline by construction.

```bash

ciss-ctl get <cid> --via s3 -o out.txt            # cross-plane fetch (same bytes)
ciss-ctl meter                                    # receipts + bytes + postage
ciss-ctl acl set <cid> --class grantees --readers id:<did>   # gate a private object
ciss-ctl sync backup ~/notes                      # chunked, dedup'd backup; only missing chunks transfer

ciss-ctl sync evict ~/notes big/video.mov         # drop local bytes (refused unless provably backed)

ciss-ctl sync status ~/notes                      # present vs evicted, cache usage, keep-set seq
ciss-ctl sync converge ~/notes                    # fold all devices' heads; conflicts preserved, never lost
```

credential, never a key. Full walkthrough: **`docs/CLIENT.md`**.
